messages:
alex: Hey team — high priority from ACME (customer-id: acme-inc). They've been hitting 429s and tail latency spikes on our Dedicated pool during a marketing-driven burst. They say they have a reserved pool (res-pool-42) and the dashboard shows spare capacity, but requests still get rate-limited. Root cause unknown. Example from their logs attached below.

maria: Sorry you're blocked, Alex. Can you paste a sample failing request/response (headers + body) and the user's observed time window? Also want to know if they're on any custom rate policy.

alex: Copied from customer:

```
Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"model":"rwd-7b-dedicated","input":"<...>","max_tokens":2048}
```

Response: 429 Too Many Requests
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Request-ID: req_0a1b2c3d
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 4
Retry-After: 4
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","scope":"project","pool":"res-pool-42"}
```

They said this happens in 30s bursts when they crank concurrency to 140. The dedicated pool has GPUs idle per the console.

devon: @alex thanks. Two common scenarios: 1) per-second token-bucket token refill is exceeded (even with idle GPUs, the per-client token quota or per-route QPS cap blocks bursts), or 2) routing fallback put them onto shared fallback tier because of transient capacity pressure during model-switch/placement.

oliver: Adding runtime details — Dedicated uses a hierarchical limiter: global cluster limiter -> pool limiter -> project limiter -> route limiter. The X-RateLimit headers are project-scoped here. If project limiter's bucket_size (burst capacity) is small, a sustained high-concurrency spike will exhaust it even if GPUs are idle (because autoscaler and placement operate in scheduling windows). Also note we throttle by "reserved_slots" not raw GPU utilization.

infra-bot: [autoscaler-event] 2026-03-15T15:12:34Z scale-up started for pool res-pool-42; requested_nodes=2, available_nodes=1 -> pending provisioning.

maria: Okay so infra saw a scale event at 15:12:34 — that matches the customer's timeline. If scaling is pending, we intentionally throttle some requests to maintain latency SLOs and avoid overload.

alex: Repro steps from customer (they gave this):
1) Use 140 concurrent connections to the generate endpoint, payload ~1k tokens.
2) Ramp up over 10s and hold for 20s.
3) Observe 429s after 6-8s and retry-after headers set.

They also tried a slower ramp (50 concurrent) and didn't hit 429s.

devon: That pattern screams "burst exceeds project bucket_size". Two immediate checks: (A) project quota config for bucket_size and refill_rate, (B) pool reserved_slots vs. active_allocations at time of spike. Can you attach the customer's project id and the pool config?

alex: Project-id: proj-acme-91. Pool config (from console snapshot):
- pool_id: res-pool-42
- reserved_slots: 8 (GPUs)
- max_instances: 16
- autoscale_cooldown: 60s
- burst_window_tokens: 40000

maria: That burst_window_tokens looks low for 140 concurrent at 1k tokens each. If each request consumes ~1k tokens, 140 * 1000 = 140k tokens in the burst. The per-project bucket won't cover that.

oliver: Confirmed. The pipeline charges tokens at request enqueue time + streaming tokens. The bucket is sized to protect multi-tenant fairness. For Dedicated customers we usually recommend increasing "burst_window_tokens" and/or enabling "burst_overprovision=true" for marketing events.

sasha: Customer-facing note: ACME is on Bronze SLA (latency priority medium). They opted not to buy extra burst add-on. They're pushing for a quick fix because this is impacting a campaign.

devon: Proposed mitigation steps (short-term):
- Increase project bucket_size (burst_window_tokens) to 200k for proj-acme-91.
- Temporarily bump reserved_slots to 12 if capacity allows in res-pool-42.
- Add a route-level rate-limit header that encourages client-side exponential backoff (we can set Retry-After and X-Backoff=serverSuggested).

oliver: Mid-term: align Dedicated SLA docs to explicitly call out how burst windows interact with autoscaler cooldowns and reserved_slots. Also add a policy to allow immediate burst scaling for customers who purchased "burst add-on".

sasha: Customer accepted temporary solution and wants a billing-friendly upgrade path. I'll open a sales ticket and coordinate.

alex: I'm going to attempt a repro from support side to validate. Quick load script I'm going to run (feel free to copy):

```
# simple k6 script-ish pseudo
for i in 1..140 {
  spawn(:http_post, url, payload)
}
sleep 20s
```

maria: If you can repro, collect /metrics from the limiter service at the time (endpoint: /internal/limiter/stats?proj=proj-acme-91) and autoscaler logs. Also capture the pool placement events (/internal/pool/placements?pool=res-pool-42&since=15:00).

infra-bot: [log] autoscaler: node-provision request queued for res-pool-42 (req_id=as_req_873)

alex: Running the load now from a support runner. Will paste results.

... 6 minutes later ...

alex: Repro confirmed. 429s start around 7s, Retry-After~4. Limiter stats snapshot:

```
/limiters/projects/proj-acme-91 -> {refill_rate: 2500 tokens/s, bucket_capacity: 40000 tokens, tokens_used_recent: 120000}
/pools/res-pool-42 -> {reserved_slots: 8, available_slots: 2, pending_nodes:2}
```

devon: That matches theory. Refill 2500 t/s with capacity 40k can't handle a 140k token burst. Even though pending_nodes=2, provisioning latency means we protect runtime by issuing 429s.

maria: Customer update draft: "We're seeing temporary rate-limit responses during very short, high-concurrency bursts because the configured burst allowance for your project is smaller than the instantaneous token demand. We can increase your burst allowance and provision more reserved slots to reduce these 429s. Temporary change requires a restart of the limiter process (5s) and config push — ETA 10 minutes." Thoughts?

sasha: Sounds fine. Add cost implication: increasing reserved_slots will increase their committed cost. Offer a one-time free trial of the burst add-on for this campaign (sales ok to approve if support confirms repro).

oliver: Operational note: we should ensure rate-limit alignment with SLA — Bronze SLA should get clearer thresholds. For now, do the config tweak and monitor. Also add a short-lived permissive override keyed to proj-acme-91 with expire=+2h to allow them to finish the campaign, then revert automatically.

devon: Action items:
- alex: run the limiter config bump and monitor (increase bucket_capacity to 200k; set refill_rate to 40000 for 2 min window) — owner: alex — ETA 10m.
- infra: expedite node provisioning for res-pool-42 or allow immediate provisional_slots for burst — owner: infra team — ETA 15m.
- sasha: confirm customer acceptance of temporary cost & trial — owner: sasha — ETA 20m.

alex: Starting config change now. I'll post logs and final status once done.

infra-bot: [action] limiter-config-push for proj-acme-91 succeeded (commit: cfg_20260315_01)

alex: Change applied. Running the same load again.

... 4 minutes later ...

alex: Post-change results: no 429s during the same burst profile. Latency stayed within Bronze SLOs. Autoscaler did add 2 nodes after ~45s. Collected metrics attached.

maria: Great. Customer-facing message approved by Sasha. I'll send the note with the two options: 1) temporary config bump (we already applied) and 2) long-term: upgrade burst add-on or increase reserved_slots permanently.

sasha: Customer accepted temporary solution and wants a billing-friendly upgrade path. I'll open a sales ticket and coordinate.

devon: Long-term follow-ups (tech backlog):
- expose a clearer per-project burst predictor in Console (estimate tokens needed for concurrency X at payload size Y).
- add an auto-tiered burst policy for Dedicated that respects purchased burst add-ons and can pre-warm nodes for planned events.

alex: Closing loop here. Will file a postmortem if anything unexpected arises. Thanks everyone. :tada:
